definitions.explanation: Meeting or interacting directly with someone in the same physical location, as opposed to online or remote communication.

examples.japanese: {対面|たいめん}で{話|はな}したい。
{対面|たいめん}での{会議|かいぎ}が{増|ふ}えてきた。
オンラインではなく{対面|たいめん}で{授業|じゅぎょう}を{受|う}けたいという{学生|がくせい}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Many students prefer to take classes in person rather than online.

notes:
USAGE:
Became especially common after the COVID-19 pandemic as a contrast to online or remote interactions. Used with で as an adverb, or with の to modify nouns ({対面|たいめん}での{授業|じゅぎょう}).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {対面|たいめん}で{会|あ}う (to meet in person)
- {対面|たいめん}で{話|はな}す (to talk face-to-face)
- {対面|たいめん}での{授業|じゅぎょう} (in-person classes)
- {対面|たいめん}での{面接|めんせつ} (in-person interview)

CONTRASTS:
- オンラインで (online)
- リモートで (remotely)
